clue.text: Food basket extremely oily when upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters are read from the bottom up

parts.note: a trug is a shallow wooden garden basket

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A picnic basket has tipped over and the oily food has spilled out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when upset' reverses the whole combination, which works because this is a down entry read from the bottom up. A trug is a traditional English garden basket.
explanation.definitionFit: Yogurt is a cultured milk product, an everyday example of food.

clue.text: Hole, see, inside cube

indicators.note: inside places the letter for see within the word for cube

parts.note: a die is a small cube used in games
V is short for vide, Latin for see, used in references

explanation.surface: A puzzle-like list: a hole, a look, and something inside a cube.
explanation.definitionFit: A dive is slang for a seedy, run-down bar or club, much like a hole or dump.

clue.text: Obsessive, perhaps, working late to circumnavigate eastern island

indicators.note: to sail round, so the first pair of words goes around the second pair

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
the late person is a dead one

explanation.surface: A sailor working late on a voyage around an island in the east.
explanation.walkthrough: The parts for 'working late' sit either side of E and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a single fixed idea is one example of an obsessive person, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Certainly, float over Everest on vacation

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the word is turned upside down, read from bottom to top

parts.note: a buoy is a float anchored in water

indicators.note: a vacated word has been emptied of its middle, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: A balloonist proposing to float over Mount Everest while on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns BUOY to YOUB; 'on vacation' leaves ET from Everest.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an informal exclamation of agreement meaning sure or of course.

clue.text: Knowing everything, minions etc. worried

indicators.note: worried in the sense of a dog worrying something, pulled about, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Followers and others fret that their boss knows everything they do.
explanation.definitionFit: All-knowing is the literal sense of the Latin-derived adjective, applied to God.

clue.text: Speculative one stopping off, so to speak, by a loch

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so the letter for one sits inside the words for off

parts.note: something that is off can be described as not on
I is the Roman numeral one
L is a map abbreviation for loch or lake

explanation.surface: Someone stopping off by a Scottish loch on a speculative trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so to speak' warns that 'off' is to be read as the phrase NOT ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Notional and speculative both describe something existing only as a theory or guess.

clue.text: Dodge, say, registration using forged clientele pass

indicators.note: forged means faked or hammered into a new shape, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone dodging registration with a forged pass for the clientele.
explanation.walkthrough: Dodge is an American car make, so the US spelling is required, and the anagram letters confirm it.
explanation.definitionFit: The registration of a car such as a Dodge is displayed on its number plates, which Americans call by this name.

clue.text: John collaring man about uniform's decorative coat?

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the combined letters are read backwards
collaring means grabbing around the neck, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: john is slang for a lavatory, a loo
MR, short for Mister, is a man's title
U is uniform in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A man called John grabs someone by the collar over the state of his uniform's coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collaring' and then 'about' both act before U is added: the reversal covers only the loo-and-mister block. The question mark flags that ormolu is a gilding rather than literally a coat.
explanation.definitionFit: This gilded bronze is used as a gold-coloured decorative finish on furniture, hence a coat in a loose sense.

clue.text: They swarm surface, maybe covering stone

indicators.note: the first word covers, that is surrounds, the abbreviation for stone

parts.note: in maths a locus is a set of points, which may form a curve or a surface
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight

explanation.surface: Insects swarm over a surface and cover a stone.
explanation.definitionFit: These grasshopper-like insects travel in vast swarms that strip crops.

clue.text: Instrument placed on nitrogen bomb

indicators.note: placed on means put next to, here following

parts.note: N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen
uke is short for ukulele, a small guitar

explanation.surface: A musical instrument is set on top of a nitrogen bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to nuke means to attack with nuclear weapons, to bomb.

clue.text: Imperceptibly close to cutting 5.08 cm

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so the word for close to sits between the two units

parts.note: an inch is 2.54 cm, so 5.08 cm is two inches
by means near or close to, as in standing by the door

explanation.surface: Something moves imperceptibly near to cutting a measurement of 5.08 cm.
explanation.walkthrough: The 5.08 cm must be read as two separate inches, split by BY.
explanation.definitionFit: Progressing in tiny steps is slow enough to be imperceptible.

clue.text: Articles about heartless Eurasian goddess

parts.note: a and the are the indefinite and definite articles

indicators.note: about means turned round, so those two letters are read backwards
with the heart removed, only the outer letters of the word remain

explanation.surface: Newspaper articles discuss a cold-hearted Eurasian goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' leaves EN from Eurasian and 'about' reverses it to NE.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the Greek deity of wisdom, also spelt Athena.

clue.text: I cycle round in match on a great circle

indicators.note: in places the reversed letters within the word for match

parts.note: to match is to equal

indicators.note: round means turned around, so I and the rota are read backwards

parts.note: a rota is a schedule that repeats in a cycle

explanation.surface: A cyclist goes round in a race on a large circular track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I cycle round' looks like a cyclist doing a lap, but 'round' turns I plus the rota backwards before 'in' places them.
explanation.definitionFit: The equator is the great circle halfway between the poles, so lying on it is equatorial.

clue.text: Mark having to produce non-U wallet

parts.note: to mark something is to note it

indicators.note: non-U means without the letter U, which is taken out

parts.note: to cause is to bring about or produce

explanation.surface: A posh person is told to produce a wallet, the word itself being not quite the done thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-U' plays on the British class label for unrefined speech, and here simply drops U from CAUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A notecase is an older term for a billfold for carrying banknotes.

clue.text: Snobs duel when ordered by head — no limits apply in this state

definitions.text: no limits apply in this state

indicators.note: by means next to, so the headland word follows
ordered means put in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour names

explanation.surface: Snobbish duellists arranged by a leader, with no limits on the fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A condition where nothing is bounded is a state of infinity or limitless extent.

clue.text: Briefly guide into benefit of a certain logic

indicators.note: into puts the shortened word within the word for benefit

parts.note: a boon is a benefit or blessing

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: to lead is to guide

explanation.surface: A short guide to the benefits of a particular kind of logic.
explanation.definitionFit: George Boole's algebra of true and false values is a branch of logic named after him.

clue.text: The bill for transport accommodated by this?

definitions.text: The bill for transport accommodated by this?

parts.words: The bill for transport accommodated by this?
parts.note: the Bill is British slang for the police, and this vehicle carries officers about

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what the invoice for travel covers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The bill' looks like an invoice; in British slang the Old Bill is the police.
explanation.definitionFit: A police patrol vehicle carries officers, the Bill, around.

clue.text: Vigorous solver getting flu shot — that's not so bad

parts.note: the solver is addressed as you

indicators.note: not means the letters of so are excluded from the pool
bad means wrongly arranged, so the remaining letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A solver who gets a flu jab finds it isn't so bad after all.
explanation.walkthrough: Take S and O out of FLUSHOT and rearrange the rest (THFUL), signalled by 'not' and 'bad'.
explanation.definitionFit: Young people are typically full of energy, so the word suggests vigour.

clue.text: Lame cattle put up on sale — just 50%?

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means raised, reading the word upwards

parts.note: beef cattle are bred for meat, so beef can mean cattle

indicators.note: just half of the word is taken, here its second half

explanation.surface: Lame cattle offered for sale at half price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' reverses BEEF to FEEB; 'just 50%' takes LE, the back half of sale.
explanation.definitionFit: A lame excuse is a weak or unconvincing one.

clue.text: Nettle sting I regularly scrat, removing top

indicators.note: removing the top means dropping the first letter

parts.note: to sting is to hurt

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter

explanation.surface: A nettle stings, so the victim keeps scratching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes CA from scrat, a dialect word for scratch.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the botanical genus name for the stinging nettle.

clue.text: America almost bombed disputed territory

indicators.note: bombed means blown apart, so the letters are scattered
almost means not quite all, dropping the last letter

explanation.surface: America nearly attacked a contested region from the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims America to AMERIC, and 'bombed' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: The peninsula on the Black Sea was annexed by Russia from Ukraine and its status is contested.

clue.text: Again seized back and leaned on

parts.note: the rear is the back
rested means leaned or lay against something

explanation.surface: Someone captured a second time, then leaned back on something.
explanation.definitionFit: Arresting someone a second time means seizing them again.

clue.text: Retreat from 13, going north

indicators.note: going north means read upwards, as 13 is a down entry
from means taken out of, so some letters are lifted from inside that answer

parts.note: the answer to 13 down is EQUATORIAL

explanation.surface: An army retreats from the equator, heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside 13 Down sit the letters RIAL; 'going north' reads them upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild animal's den is its retreat or hiding place.

clue.text: Place Israel over and above Brexit issue

indicators.note: in a down entry, above means coming before
over means turned over, so the code is read backwards

parts.note: IL is the international code for Israel
the EU, the European Union, was what Brexit was about

explanation.surface: Israel ranks a placing above the question of Brexit.
explanation.definitionFit: In lieu means in place of, so the word means place in that sense.

clue.text: Ready to work at any time, almost every

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is missing

parts.note: once can mean at any time, as in if once you falter
all can mean every, as in all people

explanation.surface: A worker is ready to work at any time, almost every day.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor available whenever summoned is on duty in this sense.

clue.text: Of average height, in the main

definitions.text: Of average height, in the main

parts.words: Of average height, in the main
parts.note: the main is the sea, and the reference height for land is the mean height of the sea's surface

explanation.surface: A person who is of average height for the most part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the main' looks like 'mostly' but means at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Altitudes are measured from the mean surface of the ocean, the baseline height.
